title: beta-sitosterol suppresses malignant biological behaviors and glycolysis via modulating YBX1-hnRNP K interaction in non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Ma, Guolu; Feng, Jianyu; Zeng, Jianying; Liao, Rongxin; Zhong, Xiaojun; Lv, Zhuo; Chen, Fengsheng
one_liner_zh: 该文研究β-谷甾醇通过调控YBX1-hnRNP K蛋白互作抑制肺癌恶性行为，虽涉及蛋白-蛋白互作和分子对接，但核心非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且方法以湿实验为主，与本课题TF-DNA结合建模关联较弱。
abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the most prevalent form of lung malignancy. As a type of phytosterol, beta-sitosterol shares structural similarities with cholesterol and has been shown to possess multiple pharmacological properties. This study aimed to investigate how beta-sitosterol influences the progression of NSCLC. To assess the impact of beta-sitosterol on NSCLC cells, a treatment with a range of concentrations was administered. Subsequent analyses included cell viability (CCK-8 assay), proliferation (EdU incorporation), migration and invasion (Transwell chambers), apoptosis (flow cytometry), and glycolytic metabolism. Interactions between Y-box binding protein 1 (YBX1) and heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein K (hnRNP K) were predicted using STRING, DMFold, and molecular docking approaches, with subsequent validation by co-immunoprecipitation. To verify their functional roles, genetic modification techniques including overexpression and knockdown were employed. beta-sitosterol dose-dependently inhibited malignant biological behaviors and glycolysis while promoting apoptosis. Notably, beta-sitosterol suppressed YBX1-hnRNP K binding without altering their expression. Moreover, YBX1 overexpression or YBX1 mutation promoted malignancy and glycolysis, whereas hnRNP K silencing reversed these effects. In this in vitro study, beta-sitosterol suppressed malignant biological behaviors and glycolysis. This effect was associated with suppressed YBX1-hnRNP K interaction in NSCLC cells. Although the precise mechanism by which beta-sitosterol disrupts this interaction remains to be elucidated, our findings identify the YBX1-hnRNP K complex as a potential mediator of beta-sitosterol's anti-tumor activity in NSCLC.
abstract_zh: 非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）是最常见的肺部恶性肿瘤类型。作为一种植物甾醇，β-谷甾醇与胆固醇在结构上具有相似性，并已被证明具有多种药理特性。本研究旨在探讨β-谷甾醇如何影响NSCLC的进展。为评估β-谷甾醇对NSCLC细胞的影响，采用了不同浓度的处理。后续分析包括细胞活力（CCK-8检测）、增殖（EdU掺入）、迁移和侵袭（Transwell小室）、凋亡（流式细胞术）以及糖酵解代谢。利用STRING、DMFold和分子对接方法预测Y-box结合蛋白1（YBX1）与异质性核糖核蛋白K（hnRNP K）之间的相互作用，并通过免疫共沉淀进行验证。为验证其功能作用，采用了过表达和敲低等遗传修饰技术。β-谷甾醇剂量依赖性地抑制恶性生物学行为和糖酵解，同时促进凋亡。值得注意的是，β-谷甾醇抑制了YBX1-hnRNP K结合，而不改变其表达。此外，YBX1过表达或YBX1突变促进了恶性和糖酵解，而hnRNP K沉默则逆转了这些效应。在本体外研究中，β-谷甾醇抑制了恶性生物学行为和糖酵解。这一效应与NSCLC细胞中YBX1-hnRNP K相互作用的抑制相关。尽管β-谷甾醇破坏这种相互作用的具体机制尚待阐明，但我们的发现将YBX1-hnRNP K复合物确定为β-谷甾醇在NSCLC中抗肿瘤活性的潜在介导因子。
